children: Adani Airports postpones the planned relocation of international operations following airline opposition, while a joint working group prepares a revised roadmap for Terminal 1 redevelopment

Adani Airports Holdings (AAHL) has deferred the proposed partial shift of international flights from Mumbai airport to Navi Mumbai International Airport until March 2027, following discussions with airline representatives over operational disruptions and the timing of the transition.

The decision means airlines will not face changes to their existing flight slots during the winter schedule, which begins on October 25 and runs until March 2027. The proposed relocation had drawn opposition from carriers concerned about the short implementation timeline and the impact on services during the busy winter travel season.

The transition is linked to the planned redevelopment of Terminal 1 (T1) at Mumbai airport. Airlines had been asked to reduce international departures by 33 per cent or shift some operations to Navi Mumbai by October 25, prompting concerns over flight schedules and the availability of a detailed redevelopment plan.
Airline Opposition Prompts Fresh Transition Plan

The decision followed a meeting on Tuesday between senior AAHL executives, including Jeet Adani and chief executive Arun Bansal, and representatives of the Airline Operators' Committee (AOC) in Mumbai.

The discussions followed a stakeholder meeting chaired by Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha on October 6, at which it was agreed that the transition plan would be discussed further with airlines.

A spokesperson for Mumbai International Airport (MIAL), which operates Mumbai airport, said the airport management had assured airlines that historical slot allocations would be respected and that no slots would be disturbed during the winter schedule.

The airport operator also said a joint working group would work over the following two weeks to develop an implementation plan for the redevelopment of T1. Airlines have committed to supporting the redevelopment and traffic balancing from the summer schedule, according to the spokesperson.

MIAL has also offered support to airlines that voluntarily wish to move some operations to Navi Mumbai. The final details of the transition plan are expected to be discussed at a meeting chaired by the civil aviation secretary on October 20, according to reports.
265 Weekly International Flights Were At Risk
MIAL had earlier asked 46 airlines operating from Mumbai airport to implement a 33 per cent reduction in international departure slots from 11.59 pm on October 25.
Of the 770 weekly international flights operating from Terminal 2 (T2), airlines had been asked to temporarily discontinue 265 weekly overseas services or shift them to Navi Mumbai.

The proposed adjustment was intended to free up capacity at T2 to accommodate domestic operations displaced by the redevelopment of T1. Mumbai airport currently operates two terminals, with T1 handling domestic flights and T2 serving international operations alongside domestic services.
The revised timeline provides airlines with additional time to plan their schedules and coordinate any eventual transfer of operations.
Terminal 1 Redevelopment May Also Be Delayed

The redevelopment of Mumbai airport's ageing T1 infrastructure is central to the proposed redistribution of flight operations. One source indicated that the entire renovation plan could also be deferred until the summer schedule begins in March 2027.

The north section of T1 is due for redevelopment, requiring passenger traffic to be accommodated through a combination of existing infrastructure and Navi Mumbai airport. The airport operator had previously said that 91 per cent of Mumbai airport's passenger traffic would remain unaffected by the planned redevelopment and subsequent relocation of some operations.

The revised transition plan is expected to be developed in consultation with airlines, with the immediate priority being to minimise disruption while addressing capacity constraints during the redevelopment.

Both Mumbai airport and Navi Mumbai International Airport are part of Adani Airports Holdings, with Mumbai airport operated by MIAL. The shift is part of a broader effort to balance traffic across the two airports as Mumbai's existing aviation infrastructure undergoes redevelopment.
